blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from Jared's verified local notes (researched November 1, 2026). Listing-stated figures are labelled; unconfirmed items say so. No live listing feed or board statistics are attached to this page yet.

South Cambie is the City of Vancouver's Cambie Street corridor between roughly West 16th Avenue and the Fraser River (Marine Drive), including the Cambie Village stretch and the area around the King Edward and Oakridge–41st stations' northern edges; the board sub-area name is "South Cambie," with nearby areas Oakridge, Riley Park, Shaughnessy, Douglas Park, Marpole and Langara.
This guide covers South Cambie's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.

Current service charge: UNCONFIRMED from public sources — OPAL operates as a retirement residence, so the service and care agreements sit on top of strata fees and must be priced from the documents, not a listing.
Parc Elise by DAVA Developments — 4488 Cambie Street (North Building) and 4408 Cambie Street

A master-planned development at the entrance to Queen Elizabeth Park: 102 units in total — 83 apartments and 19 townhomes — in two 6-storey mid-rise buildings per the developer source; the townhome component is part of this development and is not counted again below. The building directory records the North Building (4488 Cambie Street) as built 2017 with bylaws "Pets allowed w/rest., rentals allowed," while current listings at 4408 Cambie Street record year built 2019, Apartment/Condo type and the subdivision name "Parc Elise" — the two addresses carry two different built years in public records, flagged here rather than merged. A listing source describes the 4408 Cambie Street unit as a freehold apartment/condo.
528 West King Edward Avenue

A concrete building on the quiet side of Cambie and King Edward; the building directory records it as built 2019 with strata bylaws "Pets allowed, rentals allowed," while current listings record year built 2020, Apartment/Condo type and cats OK in the pet field — the built-year conflict (2019 vs 2020) is flagged, not resolved. The building carries no separate marketing name in the sources checked — it is filed under its address. Unit count: UNCONFIRMED.

items.t: South Cambie is the City of Vancouver's Cambie Street corridor between roughly West 16th Avenue and the Fraser River (Marine Drive), including the Cambie Village stretch and the area around the King Edward and Oakridge–41st stations' northern edges; the board sub-area name is "South Cambie," with nearby areas Oakridge, Riley Park, Shaughnessy, Douglas Park, Marpole and Langara.

Where the condo stock concentrates: at the King Edward Canada Line node (OPAL, 528 West King Edward Avenue) and on the Queen Elizabeth Park rise at Cambie and West 31st–35th (Parc Elise, Chelsea) — the side streets between stations are primarily houses under the R1-1 multiplex district.
Transit: the Canada Line stations at King Edward Avenue and Oakridge–41st Avenue serve the area, with Langara–49th Avenue at the corridor's south end, as set out in the Cambie Corridor Plan.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in South Cambie

items.t: Vancouver Empty Homes Tax (3%): owners must submit an annual property status declaration; the tax charges 3% of assessed value on homes declared or deemed empty, with the annual declaration due February 3, 2026 and payment due April 16, 2026. Vancouver property taxes: 2026 advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid balances.

Flood rules at the south end: the streets running down to Marine Drive sit at the edge of the Fraser River floodplain environment, and the Vancouver Building By-law's Flood Plain Standards set a minimum flood construction level of 4.6 m (GVRD datum) for new construction in designated flood plains; lot-by-lot designation must be confirmed with the City.

blocks.text: Good to know about South Cambie

items.t: OPAL spans a whole city block — and three tenures. The 130-home community between Yukon and Cambie Streets mixes 44 strata condos, 56 rentals and 30 complex-care suites in three connected buildings; two homes with the same street address can have entirely different purchase documents.
This sub-area has four tenure structures in a few blocks.

The corridor's north end is a hospital district. BC Children's Hospital and BC Women's Hospital & Health Centre at 4500 Oak Street make the campus one of the largest health-care employment and patient-trip generators on the west side — a distinct tenant and buyer pool for King Edward–area buildings.

The secondary school in the corridor is not the catchment for the corridor's west side. The VSB locator returned Eric Hamber Secondary for 500 West 20th Avenue even though Sir Winston Churchill Secondary stands inside the corridor at Heather and West 54th — catchment follows the address, not the map.

The plan, not the base zoning, drives corridor land value. The Cambie Corridor Plan (2011, Phase 3 in 2018) designations decide what a Cambie-fronting lot can become, and most of those densities still require a rezoning — price land on policy support, not as-built density.

Streets, schools and getting around South Cambie

items.t: The corridor is planned under the Cambie Corridor Plan (Council approved May 9, 2011; Phase 3, approved 2018, extended policy to the neighbourhood streets within walking distance of the Canada Line stations, adding townhouse and low-rise apartment forms off the arterial). Citywide direction now comes from the Vancouver Official Development Plan, which replaced the Vancouver Plan on March 31, 2026.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: at the station nodes, not on the side streets — and almost always inside larger developments.
Transit: Canada Line stations at King Edward Avenue and Oakridge–41st Avenue, with Langara–49th Avenue at the corridor's south end.

Schools (SD39; Ministry-listed names only): Edith Cavell Elementary (500 West 20th Avenue) is the corridor's named public elementary school; Sir Winston Churchill Secondary (7055 Heather Street) is the public secondary school located inside the corridor. The one locator run documented in the research is for 500 West 20th Avenue: Edith Cavell Elementary / Eric Hamber Secondary (SD39 School Locator, run 2026-11-01) — location is not catchment: Churchill stands in the corridor but is not that address's catchment secondary. Catchments for other addresses: UNVERIFIED.

Anchors: Queen Elizabeth Park (52 hectares, 125 metres above sea level — the highest point in the City of Vancouver), Douglas Park Community Centre (801 West 22nd Avenue), the BC Children's Hospital / BC Women's Hospital campus at 4500 Oak Street, and VanDusen Botanical Garden (5251 Oak Street, 22 hectares) at the northwest edge.

Flood edge: the streets running down to Marine Drive sit at the edge of the Fraser River floodplain environment; the Vancouver Building By-law's Flood Plain Standards and Requirements set a minimum flood construction level of 4.6 m (GVRD datum) for new construction in designated flood plains — confirm designation lot by lot with the City.

blocks.text: Good to know about South Cambie

items.t: One address, four tenures.

Parc Elise's two buildings carry two different build years in public records. The directory records the North Building at 4488 Cambie Street as built 2017, while listings at 4408 Cambie Street record 2019 — match a unit to its own building's record before comparing.

The corridor's south end has a flood number. New construction in designated flood plains at the Marine Drive end carries a minimum flood construction level of 4.6 m (GVRD datum) under the Building By-law's Flood Plain Standards — a per-lot check, not an area assumption.
The townhouse count turns on one word: "inside." Parc Elise's 19 townhomes, Chelsea's townhomes and Park Langara's townhouse units are all real townhouse floor plans — inside apartment strata.

blocks.text: Lots and land in South Cambie
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Side-street house lots: the documented stock is older detached houses on the side streets — mostly mid-century and earlier character homes on standard lots, freehold — with townhouses and 4–6 storey strata and rental buildings concentrated on Cambie Street and around the King Edward and Oakridge–41st stations under the Cambie Corridor Plan. A fee-simple lot carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees. The research states no lot-size range for the corridor, and none is invented here; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot: UNVERIFIED.

Multiplex character of the house lots: for detached-house lots away from the corridor arterials, By-law No. 13817 replaced the RS districts with the R1-1 district, allowing up to 6 strata units (or 8 secured rental units) on former single-family lots — that potential, not bare land, is what a South Cambie house-lot sale actually carries.

Serviced position: corridor homes are on City water and sewer services; a 2026 utility dollar figure confirmed on a City source: UNVERIFIED. Septic or well use in the corridor: UNVERIFIED in the research.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in South Cambie is confirmed in the research and no split is stated — ALR status is a per-parcel check on ALC mapping.

Flood position at the south end: the streets running down to Marine Drive sit at the edge of the Fraser River floodplain environment, and the Vancouver Building By-law's Flood Plain Standards and Requirements set a minimum flood construction level of 4.6 m (GVRD datum) for new construction in designated flood plains; lot-by-lot designation must be confirmed with the City.

blocks.text: Development sites and assemblies

items.t: Heather Lands — a documented rezoned development site, not lots for sale: 8.5 hectares (21.1 acres) between West 33rd and West 37th Avenues, owned by the MST Nations (Musqueam, Squamish, Tsleil-Waututh) with Canada Lands Company. Council approved the original rezoning on May 24, 2022 under the 2018 Heather Lands Policy Statement (about 2,600 homes, 4.4 acres of park); that scheme was superseded on March 31, 2026, when Council approved a replacement rezoning under the provincial Attainable Housing Initiative — 16 buildings of 4 to 46 storeys with roughly 4,200 homes, including about 2,940 discounted leasehold strata (AHI) units, about 700 market leasehold strata units and about 610 social housing units, plus a 125-space childcare, an MST Cultural Centre, a one-acre school site and over four acres of park. The future product is predominantly LEASEHOLD strata on MST/CLC land — a development site in build-out, documented here as such; no lot in it is bare-land inventory, and construction phasing / first occupancy dates are UNVERIFIED.

Oakridge Municipal Town Centre: the corridor's growth framework targets the Oakridge Municipal Town Centre at 41st and Cambie as its southern anchor, with new housing in townhouse and medium- to higher-density forms along the corridor — plan policy for assembled station-area parcels, not a lot offering.

Assemblies generally: the research's documented position is that on or near Cambie Street the Cambie Corridor Plan — not just base zoning — drives value, and plan designation must be distinguished from approved zoning because most corridor densities still require a rezoning application; price land on policy support, not as-built density. No specific assembly is named as for-sale inventory in the research.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around South Cambie

items.t: The corridor is planned under the Cambie Corridor Plan: Council approved it on May 9, 2011 to guide transit-oriented growth along Cambie Street from 16th Avenue to the Fraser River, centred on the Canada Line stations at Marine Drive, Langara–49th Avenue, Oakridge–41st Avenue and King Edward; Phase 3 (approved 2018) extended land-use policy to the neighbourhood streets within walking distance of the stations, adding townhouse and low-rise apartment forms off the arterial.

Landmarks and anchors: Queen Elizabeth Park (52 hectares at 125 metres above sea level — the highest point in the City of Vancouver) anchors the east side; Douglas Park Community Centre is at 801 West 22nd Avenue; BC Children's Hospital and BC Women's Hospital & Health Centre share the campus at 4500 Oak Street on the west side; VanDusen Botanical Garden (5251 Oak Street, 22 hectares) sits at the northwest edge; Langara College sits at the corridor's south end at West 49th Avenue.

Schools: public schools are run by the Vancouver School Board (SD39). The corridor's named public elementary school is Edith Cavell Elementary (500 West 20th Avenue); Sir Winston Churchill Secondary (7055 Heather Street) is the public secondary school located inside the corridor. Location is not catchment: the SD39 locator run documented in the research — for the single sample address 500 West 20th Avenue only — returns Edith Cavell Elementary / Eric Hamber Secondary; that single-address result does not transfer to other corridor addresses, and all other catchments are UNVERIFIED.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in South Cambie

items.t: Plan framework — Cambie Corridor Plan (2011; Phase 3, 2018): the corridor's growth framework, centred on the Canada Line stations; most corridor densities still require a rezoning application, so a plan designation is policy support, not zoning.
Citywide direction — Vancouver Official Development Plan: the Vancouver Plan was replaced by the Vancouver Official Development Plan on March 31, 2026.

Zoning / SSMUH — R1-1 multiplex district (By-law No. 13817): the RS districts were replaced with R1-1, allowing up to 6 strata units (or 8 secured rental units) on former single-family lots, subject to the district schedule. Corridor arterial and station-area parcels sit under corridor designations and site-specific districts rather than R1-1 — confirm the parcel's district with the City.

Flood construction level: minimum 4.6 m (GVRD datum) for new construction in designated flood plains under the Vancouver Building By-law's Flood Plain Standards and Requirements, based on a coastal flood risk assessment that considered 1 m of sea level rise; confirm whether the specific lot is designated.

ALR rules (for completeness — no South Cambie ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR, and no flat line is asserted for this area.

Empty Homes Tax — Vancouver only: the City charges 3% of assessed taxable value on homes declared or deemed empty; the annual declaration was due February 3, 2026 and payment April 16, 2026. A vacant house-lot held empty is the land-buyer exposure here; the tax is a City of Vancouver tax and applies in South Cambie.
Purchase prohibition / speculation taxes beyond the above: No other speculation/vacancy position is documented in the research.

blocks.text: Good to know about South Cambie

items.t: The corridor's biggest land story is leasehold, not freehold: the Heather Lands replacement rezoning (March 31, 2026) roughly doubled the site's homes — from about 2,600 in the 2022 scheme to roughly 4,200 — and the product is predominantly discounted leasehold strata under the provincial Attainable Housing Initiative, with a one-acre school site for the Conseil Scolaire Francophone and an MST Cultural Centre in the scheme. A buyer comparing a future Heather Lands unit against a freehold Cambie lot is comparing two different tenures.

Four ownership structures sit inside one sub-area: the research records freehold side-street houses, strata corridor apartments and townhouses, purpose-built rental buildings, and predominantly leasehold future strata at Heather Lands — four different ownership structures within South Cambie, which is why tenure is the first question on any corridor purchase.

The secondary school inside the corridor is not the catchment for the sample address beside it: the SD39 locator run for 500 West 20th Avenue returns Eric Hamber Secondary, not Sir Winston Churchill Secondary at Heather and West 54th — location is not catchment, and the run is single-address only.

Queen Elizabeth Park is the city's high point: 52 hectares at 125 metres above sea level, the highest point in the City of Vancouver, with the Bloedel Conservatory, quarry gardens and an arboretum — the recreation anchor for the corridor's whole east side, and part of why the east-side side streets price as house lots, not development scraps.

faq.q: Is OPAL a normal condo purchase?
faq.a: Only partly: OPAL is a 130-home retirement community of which 44 homes are strata condos (the rest are rental and complex-care suites), built 2019, with a 55+ requirement ("One resident must be 55+") and retirement-residence services — read the service and care agreements, not just the Form B, and note the current service charge is UNCONFIRMED from public sources.

faq.q: Can I rent out a South Cambie condo long-term?
faq.a: Yes — rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022, and the directories for Parc Elise and 528 West King Edward state rentals allowed. Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax declaration (3%) still applies if the unit sits empty instead.

faq.q: Why do Parc Elise addresses show two different built years?
faq.a: Public records split by address: the directory records the North Building at 4488 Cambie Street as built 2017, while listings at 4408 Cambie Street record 2019. The development totals 102 units (83 apartments, 19 townhomes) across two 6-storey buildings — match a unit to its own building's record before comparing.

faq.q: What is the Heather Lands and will its homes be freehold?
faq.a: No — the 8.5-hectare Heather Street site (MST Nations with Canada Lands Company) was rezoned March 31, 2026 for roughly 4,200 homes, predominantly discounted and market leasehold strata. Price and finance any future purchase there as leasehold from the first conversation.

faq.q: Which station is my building actually near?
faq.a: OPAL and 528 West King Edward sit at the King Edward station node; Parc Elise and Chelsea sit between King Edward and Oakridge–41st, at the Queen Elizabeth Park rise. Name the station in any offer — "Cambie corridor" alone spans four stations.

faq.q: What townhouse complexes can I actually buy in South Cambie?
faq.a: Inside this sub-area's own developments, townhouse-form units exist at Parc Elise (19 of 102 units), Chelsea (within its 79 homes) and Park Langara — all strata lots in apartment developments, bought as condos.

faq.q: Are the Parc Elise or Chelsea townhomes a separate townhouse strata?
faq.a: No — each is a townhouse-form stratum inside one apartment development (Parc Elise: 83 apartments + 19 townhomes; Chelsea: 79 flats and townhomes in two six-storey buildings). You buy under that development's single strata plan and Form B; there is no separate townhouse corporation.
